validated_results.title: Vitamin D Supplements and Prevention of Cancer and Cardiovascular Disease.
validated_results.journal: The New England journal of medicine
validated_results.reason: This randomized controlled trial reports the effect of vitamin D supplementation on incident prostate cancer risk.

sample_size.excerpt: Of the 25,871 participants, 51% were women and mean age was 67.1 years. The cohort was racially diverse, with 71% self-declared non-Hispanic whites, 20% African Americans, and the rest, members of other racial/ethnic groups.

effect_size.excerpt: For secondary endpoints, the hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals comparing Vitamin D to placebo were: cancer deaths (n=341, HR 0.83 (0.67–1.02); breast cancer (1.02; 0.79–1.31); prostate cancer 0.88 (0.72–1.07); colorectal cancer 1.09 (0.73–1.62); expanded cardiovascular disease events 0.96 (0.86–1.08); myocardial infarction 0.96 (0.78–1.19); stroke 0.95 (0.76–1.20); and cardiovascular mortality 1.11 (0.88–1.40).

confidence_interval.excerpt: For secondary endpoints, the hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals comparing Vitamin D to placebo were: cancer deaths (n=341, HR 0.83 (0.67–1.02); breast cancer (1.02; 0.79–1.31); prostate cancer 0.88 (0.72–1.07); colorectal cancer 1.09 (0.73–1.62); expanded cardiovascular disease events 0.96 (0.86–1.08); myocardial infarction 0.96 (0.78–1.19); stroke 0.95 (0.76–1.20); and cardiovascular mortality 1.11 (0.88–1.40).
